fill.description: orbit: fraction of the frame the target fills (default 0.7)

tools.description:
Record and compare the editor level (files under Saved/MCP/snapshots).
- op=take: store `name` (default auto) — actors matched by object path, with class, tags, transform.
- op=diff: `name` vs `against` (default: the level now) → added, removed, moved, retagged; under World Partition, actors in a cell that was not loaded are `unknown`, never removed.
- op=list: stored snapshots.
- op=digest: a quantized SHA1 over actor (scope=actors) or ISM/HISM instance transforms — verify a level hashes to an expected value. Does not store anything.
Undo moves with snapshot_restore.

against.description: diff: the AFTER snapshot (default: the level right now)

class_filter.description: take/digest scope=actors: only actors whose class or label contains this

limit.description: digest scope=instances: max instances hashed (default 5,000,000; a larger set fails rather than hashing part of it)

mesh.description: digest scope=instances: mesh path substring filter

name.description: take: snapshot name (default auto; overwrites); diff: the BEFORE snapshot

pos_bucket.description: digest: position quantization in world units (default 1)

tools.name: snapshot
tools.title: Level snapshots

tools.description: Move every actor that still exists back to its transform in snapshot `name` (matched by object path; parents before attached children), as one undo step, then save. TRANSFORMS ONLY: actors spawned since are not deleted and deleted actors are not recreated — both are listed in not_restored {added, removed} (and, under World Partition, `unknown` for actors in cells that are not loaded). For those use scene_clear or git_revert.

tools.title: Restore a snapshot

The editor viewport camera and selection (UI state; nothing is saved).
- op=get: camera {location, rotation} + game_view.
- op=set: location/rotation, pilot (actor) or eject, game_view.
- op=focus: aim the camera at `actors` (default: the selection).
- op=select: select `actors` (mode replace|add|remove|none), frame=true to focus them.
- op=selection: the selected actors (label, path, class).
Console commands moved to the console tool.

actors.description: focus/select: actor labels or object paths (focus default: the current selection)

distance_scale.description: focus: multiplier on the framing distance (default 2)

game_view.description: set: Game View on/off (hides editor-only actors, like pressing G)

pilot.description: set: pilot this actor (label or object path) with the camera

pitch.description: focus: camera pitch in degrees (default -30, negative looks down)

rotation.description: set: camera [pitch, yaw, roll] in degrees

tools.description:
Author a WidgetBlueprint's tree declaratively (create the asset with asset_create kind=widget_blueprint).
- op=compose: apply `tree` — add/update/reorder nodes, slots, props — then compile; never deletes. Re-composing the same tree is a no-op (same digest).
- op=prune: like compose, but DELETES every node absent from `tree` and the names in `remove`.
- op=compile: compile + save; returns the digest (and ends a deferred patch).
Check the result with widget_query op=tree / op=render.

defer.description: compose mode=patch: apply without compiling until op=compile

mode.description: compose: full (default; converge the whole tree on the spec, never deleting) | patch (only the given nodes)

remove.description: prune: also remove these named nodes

tree.description: compose/prune: declarative node {name, class, slot?, props?, brush?, font?, is_variable?, children?[]}; every node named; class is a friendly name (TextBlock, ProgressBar, Image, Button, CanvasPanel, VerticalBox, Overlay, ...) or a /Script or /Game path

tools.description:
Inspect UMG widgets without PIE.
- op=tree: a WidgetBlueprint's tree as JSON + digest (compare digests to verify an edit).
- op=describe: the authorable palette (no class) or a class's editable props and slot type.
- op=render: SEE a UserWidget class — offscreen PNG (needs the plugin's MCPAuthoring module; writes Saved/MCP/WidgetRenders).

class.description: describe: a widget class (omit for the whole palette); render: the UserWidget class, e.g. /Script/MyGame.HudWidget or /Game/UI/WBP_HUD.WBP_HUD_C

tools.description: Capture a specific on-screen window as a PNG — defaults to auto-detecting the Unreal Editor. Sees the FULL editor: menus, panels, the Content Browser, modal dialogs, the composited viewport with UI. method=print (default) works even when the window is backgrounded/occluded and does not steal focus; method=screen blits its on-screen rectangle. Returns the window's screen bounds so you can map image pixels to mouse_control coordinates.

focus.description: bring the window to the foreground before capturing

hwnd.description: target an exact window handle (from list_windows)

max_width.description: downscale to at most this width; default 1600, 0 = full resolution

method.description: auto|print|screen. print (default) renders the window even when backgrounded/occluded and never steals focus; screen blits its on-screen rectangle (window must be visible)

pid.description: target a specific process id instead of by title

title.description: window title substring (case-insensitive); omit to auto-detect the Unreal Editor
